items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: Bud Farrington, who was the drummer in our group

ctx.x: It was much more jazz oriented at that time. Just like what’s jazz? I mean it’s — the definition of jazz now has gotten so absurd that there are players that are supposedly qualified as jazz players that aren’t jazz players at all. And their music isn’t jazz. We don’t need to go into that. There are too many of them. But I stayed in the Conservatory for two years. The second year I was a composition major with Jed Cooke, and a piano minor. And I kept studying bass, and I had choir. Choral was conducted by a woman…

that played all the Brandenberg concerti plus Haydn and Mozart symphonies, and we had a marching band and a jazz band. An amazing — Newton High School was like the number three high school in the country at one point there. And that’s where Sudhalter and I went to school, and most of this band. Bud Farrington, who was the drummer in our group who ended up to be a Major General I think it’s called, or Brigadier General, Vietnam and all that.

So you went to the guidance counselor at Newton High School and she says, “What do you want to do?” At that point in your musical development did you have a specific idea of how you wanted to make your living in music?
